1	# Almanac nutrition pipeline
2	
3	Builds the calorie reference database from the licence-cleared food-composition
4	sources in the food-data lake (`~/ALManac-food-data`, override with
5	`ALMANAC_FOOD_DATA` or `--lake`). This file is the contract every stage and
6	every source module honours. The design it implements is
7	`~/ALManac-food-data/PROCESSING_DESIGN.md` (Processing Design v0.1); section
8	references below (§n) point there.
9	
10	## Scope of this phase
11	
12	| Source | Namespace | Group | What is canonicalised |
13	|---|---|---|---|
14	| USDA FoodData Central 2026-04-30 | `usda` | A | Foundation Foods listed in `foundation_food.csv` (395). Branded, SR Legacy, FNDDS and the 74 unlisted Foundation records are extracted or left in raw, not canonicalised. |
15	| ANSES-CIQUAL 2025 | `ciqual` | B | All 3,484 foods |
16	| CoFID 2021 | `cofid` | B | All 2,887 rows of `1.3 Proximates` |
17	| AFCD Release 3 | `afcd` | B | All 1,588 foods, per 100 g and (213 liquids) per 100 mL |
18	| Almanac-native | `almanac` | N | Nothing yet — awaits Saudi/Gulf dish data |
19	
20	Canonical nutrients are only what calorie calculation needs (energy, protein,
21	fat, carbohydrate, fibre, alcohol). The dictionary splits some of these into
22	more than one canonical nutrient where sources publish different quantities
23	under the same name — see "Carbohydrate" below.
24	
25	Group C and D sources (Open Food Facts, SFDA, NEVO, TBCA, IFCT, FAO/INFOODS,
26	Bahrain, Tunisia, Lebanon, INNTA) are never read by this pipeline.
27	
28	## Stages
29	
30	```
31	raw/  (0444, checksummed in manifests/)
32	  │ extract       per source; verifies every input's sha256 against the
33	  │               collection manifest first; no renaming, no typing
34	processed/extracted/{namespace}/     source's own shape, every cell a string
35	  │ canonicalise  per source, still separate; applies dictionary/ only
36	processed/canonical/{namespace}/     foods.csv, food_names.csv, values.csv, manifest.json
37	  │ union         every canonical/{namespace}/ present, re-validated
38	processed/union/
39	  │ bundle        the licence assertion, then SQLite
40	build/almanac.sqlite
41	```
42	
43	Each stage writes only its own directory, via a scratch directory that
44	replaces the previous output only when the stage finishes (`lake.staged_directory`).
45	Deleting any `canonical/{namespace}/` and re-running `union` + `bundle` removes
46	that source completely — the property §5 exists to protect.
47	
48	```sh
49	cd tools/nutrition
50	python3 -m almanac_nutrition extract usda        # or ciqual | cofid | afcd
51	python3 -m almanac_nutrition canonicalise usda
52	python3 -m almanac_nutrition union
53	python3 -m almanac_nutrition bundle
54	python3 -m almanac_nutrition all                 # every source, then union + bundle
55	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests            # fast; synthetic fixtures only
56	ALMANAC_NUTRITION_INTEGRATION=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests   # + real lake
57	```
58	
59	Needs Python ≥ 3.11 with `openpyxl` and `lxml`. Nothing else.
60	
61	## Dictionary — data, not code (`dictionary/`)
62	
63	| File | Holds |
64	|---|---|
65	| `nutrients.csv` | Canonical nutrients: `nutrient_id`, INFOODS tag, name, unit, description. |
66	| `nutrient_map.csv` | `(source, source_nutrient_id) → nutrient_id`, with `priority` (when several source columns feed one canonical nutrient), `unit_conversion` (`""` or `kj_to_kcal`), and `numeric_qualifier_override`. |
67	| `qualifiers.csv` | The closed qualifier vocabulary (§2) and, per qualifier, whether an amount is `null` or `required`. Must equal `NutrientQualifier` in AlmanacCore — a Swift test checks this. |
68	| `licence_groups.csv` | A, B, C, D, N and whether each may ship. Must agree with `LicenceGroup.isShippable` — a Swift test checks this. |
69	| `sources.csv` | One row per namespace: dataset id, release, licence, licence group, attribution text. The licence group of every row is taken from here, never from a source module. |
70	| `derivation_qualifiers.csv` | A source's own per-value derivation code → qualifier (USDA's 80 codes; AFCD's food-level derivation). |
71	| `value_tokens.csv` | Exact non-numeric cell tokens → qualifier (`cofid Tr`, `cofid N`, `ciqual traces`, `ciqual -`). Tokens may only map to qualifiers whose amount is `null`. |
72	
73	`dictionary.load()` cross-checks all seven and fails with every problem at
74	once. Its SHA-256 is recorded in every canonical manifest; `union` refuses a
75	canonical directory built against a different dictionary.
76	
77	## Canonical format (`processed/canonical/{namespace}/`)
78	
79	UTF-8 CSV, header row, `\n` line endings, rows sorted by key. Empty string
80	means absent.
81	
82	`foods.csv` — `food_ref, namespace, local_id, licence_group, food_group_code, food_group_name, source_record`
83	- `food_ref` is `namespace:local_id` (§3). `local_id` is the publisher's
84	  identifier, verbatim. If a publisher repeats an identifier within one
85	  release, **every** occurrence becomes `{id}@row{n}` (`n` = spreadsheet row);
86	  nothing is dropped or merged. (CoFID 2021 reuses `13-669` for two foods.)
87	- `licence_group` must equal `sources.csv` for the namespace.
88	- `source_record` says where the row came from (`food.csv fdc_id=321358`,
89	  `1.3 Proximates!row 674`, …).
90	
91	`food_names.csv` — `food_ref, language, name, is_primary`
92	- One name per language; exactly one primary (`1`) per food. Languages are
93	  lower-case ISO 639 codes (`en`, `fr`, later `ar`).
94	
95	`values.csv` — `food_ref, nutrient_id, basis, amount, qualifier, confidence, source_value, source_nutrient_id, source_unit, licence_group`
96	- The value model of §2 plus `basis`. Unique on `(food_ref, nutrient_id, basis)`.
97	- `basis` is `per_100g` or `per_100ml` — a column, never an assumption (§4).
98	- `amount` is in the canonical unit, `repr(float)`, empty only for
99	  qualifiers whose amount rule is `null` (`trace`, `not_analysed`).
100	- `source_value` is the original cell, unparsed (whitespace trimmed; XLSX
101	  numeric cells as the shortest round-trip decimal of the stored double).
102	  It is never empty.
103	- `source_nutrient_id` / `source_unit` are the source's own, verbatim.
104	- `confidence` is the source's own per-value quality or derivation marker,
105	  verbatim: USDA derivation code (`A`, `NC`), CIQUAL `code_confiance` (`A`–`D`),
106	  AFCD food-level derivation (`Analysed`), empty for CoFID.
107	
108	`manifest.json` — namespace, dataset, release, licence group, dictionary
109	SHA-256, inputs with SHA-256, output SHA-256s, counts by nutrient / qualifier /
110	basis, and `notes` (exclusions with reasons, collisions, anything a reviewer
111	must see).
112	
113	### Blank cells produce no row
114	
115	A blank cell (or an absent USDA `food_nutrient` row) means the source says
116	nothing, and produces **no value row**. A token that says "no number" (`N`,
117	`-`) produces a row with `amount` empty. Those are different facts and both
118	survive.
119	
120	## Qualifying a value — one function, in this order (`values.qualify`)
121	
122	1. Exact token from `value_tokens.csv` → that qualifier, `amount` empty.
123	   **A token never becomes 0.**
124	2. Bound prefix (CIQUAL `< x`) → `below_loq`, `amount` = x (the bound).
125	3. Anything that is not a plain finite decimal → **the stage fails**
126	   (`UnrecognisedValue`). No cell is guessed at. The one exception is a
127	   negative number (`NegativeAmount`): it is not a quantity, so it produces
128	   no row and the source module records it in `notes.rejected_values`. It is
129	   never stored and never clamped to 0. (USDA publishes negative
130	   "carbohydrate, by difference" when the other proximates exceed 100 g.)
131	4. Explicit zero → `zero_reported`, `amount` 0.
132	5. `numeric_qualifier_override` from the mapping row (all published energy
133	   values are `calculated_factor` — no food table measures energy).
134	6. The source's derivation code via `derivation_qualifiers.csv`.
135	7. Otherwise `measured`.
136	
137	Then `unit_conversion` (kJ → kcal is ÷ 4.184). Where several source columns
138	map to one canonical nutrient, the lowest `priority` that carries a quantity
139	wins; if none does, the lowest priority's marker is kept (`values.select`).
140	
141	Every canonical row set is re-validated before it is written
142	(`model.validate`), including an independent check that **an amount of 0
143	only ever comes from a cell that says 0**.
144	
145	## Source rules
146	
147	### USDA (`sources/usda.py`) — reference implementation
148	- Inputs: `FoodData Central United States/FoodData_Central_csv_2026-04-30/*.csv`
149	  (manifest `usda`).
150	- Extract: `food.csv` rows with `data_type = foundation_food` (469), their
151	  `food_nutrient` and `food_portion` rows, plus the lookup tables whole.
152	- Canonicalise: foods listed in `foundation_food.csv` (395). The other 74 are
153	  recorded in `manifest.json` `notes.excluded` (68 share a description with a
154	  listed record — superseded versions). Values per 100 g; qualifier from
155	  `derivation_id` → code → `derivation_qualifiers.csv`; blank code →
156	  `measured` (Foundation Foods are analytical); `confidence` = the code.
157	
158	### CIQUAL (`sources/ciqual.py`)
159	- Inputs: `raw/ciqual/2025/{alim,alim_grp,compo,const,sources}_2025_11_03.xml`
160	  (UTF-8 with BOM, CRLF). Extract each to CSV, one column per element, text
161	  trimmed, `missing=" "` → empty.
162	- Foods: every `alim_code`; names `en` (primary, `alim_nom_eng`) and `fr`.
163	- Values: `teneur` of mapped `const_code`s; decimal comma; tokens `traces`,
164	  `-`; `< x` → `below_loq`; `confidence` = `code_confiance`. Per 100 g.
165	
166	### CoFID (`sources/cofid.py`)
167	- Inputs: `raw/cofid/2021/McCance_Widdowsons_Composition_of_Foods_Integrated_Dataset_2021.xlsx`.
168	  Extract every sheet verbatim (all three header rows kept).
169	- Foods: `1.3 Proximates` rows 4+ with a Food Code; name `en`; group code.
170	- Columns are identified by the code row (row 2: `KCALS`, `PROT`, `FAT`,
171	  `CHO`, `AOACFIB`, `ALCO`). `Tr` → `trace`, `N` → `not_analysed`, blank → no
172	  row. Bracketed values `(0.07)` appear only in fatty-acid sheets; one in a
173	  mapped column fails the stage.
174	- Basis: `per_100ml` for group codes starting `Q` (alcoholic beverages; user
175	  guide p.7), otherwise `per_100g`.
176	
177	### AFCD (`sources/afcd.py`)
178	- Inputs: `raw/ausnut/release-3/*.xlsx` (manifest `ausnut`). Extract every sheet.
179	- Foods: `All solids & liquids per 100 g`; name `en`; `Classification` code.
180	- Values from that sheet (`per_100g`) and from `Liquids only per 100 mL`
181	  (`per_100ml`). Columns identified by header text with whitespace collapsed.
182	  Qualifier from the food-level `Derivation` via `derivation_qualifiers.csv`;
183	  `confidence` = that derivation. Energy is kJ → kcal.
184	
185	## Licence guard and bundle
186	
187	`bundle` fails the build — before any output exists — if any food or value
188	row has a licence group outside `licence_groups.csv` `shippable = true`
189	(A, B, N), or a licence group that disagrees with `sources.csv` for its
190	namespace. It then re-checks the written database and runs
191	`integrity_check` / `foreign_key_check`. The bundle's own tables also carry
192	`CHECK (licence_group IN ('A','B','N'))`, so a restricted row cannot be
193	inserted into it by any route.
194	
195	Bundle schema version 1 (`bundle.schema_sql`): `bundle_meta`,
196	`nutrition_source`, `nutrition_nutrient`, `nutrition_qualifier`,
197	`nutrition_food`, `nutrition_food_name`, `nutrition_value`. AlmanacCore's
198	`NutritionReferenceImporter` reads exactly this and re-asserts the licence
199	groups itself.
200	
201	## Energy: stored vs calculated
202	
203	The bundle stores what publishers said: `energy_kcal` (each publisher's
204	headline figure, using its own factors — not comparable across publishers)
205	and `energy_general_atwater_kcal` (USDA's own general-Atwater figure).
206	Almanac's calorie number — general Atwater, 4/4/9/7 kcal/g — is calculated in
207	AlmanacCore (`GeneralAtwater`), not here, so native entries and reference
208	foods go through one implementation.
209	
210	### Carbohydrate
211	
212	General Atwater applies 4 kcal/g to **total** carbohydrate (by difference,
213	fibre included). Sources publish different quantities under "carbohydrate",
214	so the dictionary keeps them apart:
215	
216	| Canonical | Meaning | From |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| `carbohydrate_by_difference` | total, fibre included | USDA 1005 |
219	| `carbohydrate_available` | sugars + starch by weight, no fibre | CIQUAL 31000, AFCD, USDA 1050 |
220	| `carbohydrate_available_monosaccharide` | same, as monosaccharide equivalents | CoFID CHO |
221	| `fibre_total_dietary` | AOAC total dietary fibre | USDA 1079/2033, CIQUAL, CoFID AOACFIB, AFCD |
222	
223	Collapsing them into one "carbohydrate" would under-count every fibre-rich
224	food outside USDA by 4 kcal per gram of fibre. CoFID's Englyst NSP is a
225	different measurement and is not mapped.
226

1	"""The food-data lake on disk (Processing Design v0.1 §5).
2	
3	    raw/                         immutable, verified against manifests/
4	    processed/extracted/{ns}/    the source's own shape
5	    processed/canonical/{ns}/    Almanac schema, source values preserved
6	    processed/union/             every canonical source, licence-tagged
7	    build/almanac.sqlite         what ships
8	
9	Every stage writes only its own directory, through `staged_directory`, so a
10	failed run leaves the previous output exactly as it was.
11	"""
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import csv
15	import hashlib
16	import json
17	import os
18	import shutil
19	import subprocess
20	from contextlib import contextmanager
21	from datetime import datetime, timezone
22	from pathlib import Path
23	from typing import Iterable, Iterator
24	
25	DEFAULT_ROOT = Path.home() / "ALManac-food-data"
26	
27	
28	class InputVerificationError(RuntimeError):
29	    """An input differs from what the collection manifest recorded."""
30	
31	
32	def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
33	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
34	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
35	        while block := f.read(1 << 20):
36	            digest.update(block)
37	    return digest.hexdigest()
38	
39	
40	def utc_now() -> str:
41	    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
42	
43	
44	def tool_revision() -> str:
45	    """The git commit this pipeline ran from, marked dirty if uncommitted."""
46	    here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
47	    try:
48	        head = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=here, capture_output=True,
49	                              text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
50	        dirty = subprocess.run(["git", "status", "--porcelain", "--", "."], cwd=here.parent,
51	                               capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
52	    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
53	        return "unknown"
54	    return head + ("+dirty" if dirty else "")
55	
56	
57	class Lake:
58	    def __init__(self, root: Path | str | None = None) -> None:
59	        chosen = root or os.environ.get("ALMANAC_FOOD_DATA") or DEFAULT_ROOT
60	        self.root = Path(chosen).expanduser().resolve()
61	
62	    @property
63	    def manifests(self) -> Path:
64	        return self.root / "manifests"
65	
66	    @property
67	    def canonical_root(self) -> Path:
68	        return self.root / "processed" / "canonical"
69

71	        return self.root / "processed" / "extracted" / namespace

73	    def canonical(self, namespace: str) -> Path:
74	        return self.canonical_root / namespace

76	    @property
77	    def union(self) -> Path:
78	        return self.root / "processed" / "union"
79	
80	    @property
81	    def bundle(self) -> Path:
82	        return self.root / "build" / "almanac.sqlite"

84	    def manifest(self, name: str) -> dict:
85	        return json.loads((self.manifests / f"{name}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
86	
87	    def source_dir(self, manifest_name: str) -> Path:
88	        return self.root / self.manifest(manifest_name)["local_path"]
89	
90	    def verify_inputs(self, manifest_name: str, filenames: Iterable[str]) -> list[dict]:
91	        """Checksums every input against the collection manifest before it is read."""
92	        manifest = self.manifest(manifest_name)
93	        recorded = {entry["filename"]: entry for entry in manifest["files"]}
94	        base = self.root / manifest["local_path"]
95	        verified = []
96	        for name in filenames:
97	            entry = recorded.get(name)
98	            if entry is None:
99	                raise InputVerificationError(f"{name} is not recorded in manifests/{manifest_name}.json")
100	            path = base / name
101	            if not path.is_file():
102	                raise InputVerificationError(f"{path} is missing")
103	            actual = sha256_file(path)
104	            if actual != entry["sha256"]:
105	                raise InputVerificationError(
106	                    f"{path}: sha256 {actual} differs from the manifest's {entry['sha256']}")
107	            verified.append({"file": str(path.relative_to(self.root)), "sha256": actual})
108	        return verified

111	@contextmanager
112	def staged_directory(final: Path) -> Iterator[Path]:
113	    """Yields an empty scratch directory that replaces `final` only on success."""
114	    final = Path(final)
115	    final.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
116	    scratch = final.with_name(f".{final.name}.partial")
117	    if scratch.exists():
118	        shutil.rmtree(scratch)
119	    scratch.mkdir()
120	    try:
121	        yield scratch
122	    except BaseException:
123	        shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
124	        raise
125	    retired = final.with_name(f".{final.name}.retired")
126	    if retired.exists():
127	        shutil.rmtree(retired)
128	    if final.exists():
129	        final.rename(retired)
130	    scratch.rename(final)
131	    shutil.rmtree(retired, ignore_errors=True)

1	"""The nutrient dictionary, qualifier vocabulary and licence registry — as data.
2	
3	Processing Design v0.1 §6: the mapping "will be wrong in places on the first
4	pass. Keeping it as data means fixing it is an update, not a re-extraction."
5	Nothing in the pipeline hard-codes a nutrient, a qualifier or a licence group;
6	it all comes from ../dictionary/, cross-checked here.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import csv
11	import hashlib
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	from pathlib import Path
14	
15	DICTIONARY_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "dictionary"
16	FILES = ("nutrients.csv", "qualifiers.csv", "licence_groups.csv", "sources.csv",
17	         "nutrient_map.csv", "derivation_qualifiers.csv", "value_tokens.csv")
18	
19	# unit_conversion name -> (source unit, canonical unit), compared case-insensitively.
20	# The empty name is the identity: the two units must already agree.
21	UNIT_CONVERSIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, str] | None] = {"": None, "kj_to_kcal": ("kj", "kcal")}
22	
23	
24	class DictionaryError(ValueError):
25	    """The dictionary contradicts itself. The message lists every problem."""
26	
27	
28	@dataclass(frozen=True)
29	class Nutrient:
30	    nutrient_id: str
31	    infoods_tag: str
32	    name: str
33	    unit: str
34	    description: str
35	
36	
37	@dataclass(frozen=True)
38	class Qualifier:
39	    qualifier: str
40	    has_quantity: bool
41	    directly_observed: bool
42	    amount_rule: str  # "null": amount is always empty; "required": amount is always present
43	    description: str
44	
45	
46	@dataclass(frozen=True)
47	class LicenceGroup:
48	    licence_group: str
49	    name: str
50	    shippable: bool
51	    description: str
52	
53	
54	@dataclass(frozen=True)
55	class Source:
56	    namespace: str
57	    dataset_id: str
58	    name: str
59	    release: str
60	    licence: str
61	    licence_group: str
62	    attribution: str
63	    url: str
64	
65	
66	@dataclass(frozen=True)
67	class Mapping:
68	    source: str
69	    source_nutrient_id: str
70	    source_nutrient_name: str
71	    source_unit: str
72	    nutrient_id: str
73	    priority: int
74	    unit_conversion: str
75	    numeric_qualifier_override: str
76	    notes: str
77	
78	
79	@dataclass(frozen=True)
80	class Dictionary:
81	    nutrients: dict[str, Nutrient]
82	    qualifiers: dict[str, Qualifier]
83	    licence_groups: dict[str, LicenceGroup]
84	    sources: dict[str, Source]
85	    mappings: tuple[Mapping, ...]
86	    derivations: dict[tuple[str, str], str]  # (source, code) -> qualifier
87	    tokens: dict[tuple[str, str], str]  # (source, exact cell text) -> qualifier
88	    sha256: str
89	
90	    @property
91	    def shippable_groups(self) -> frozenset[str]:
92	        return frozenset(g for g, row in self.licence_groups.items() if row.shippable)
93	
94	    def group_of(self, namespace: str) -> str:
95	        return self.sources[namespace].licence_group
96	
97	    def mappings_for(self, source: str) -> dict[str, list[Mapping]]:
98	        """Canonical nutrient -> the source's mappings for it, highest priority first."""
99	        grouped: dict[str, list[Mapping]] = {}
100	        for mapping in self.mappings:
101	            if mapping.source == source:
102	                grouped.setdefault(mapping.nutrient_id, []).append(mapping)
103	        return {n: sorted(ms, key=lambda m: m.priority) for n, ms in sorted(grouped.items())}
104	
105	    def tokens_for(self, source: str) -> dict[str, str]:
106	        return {token: q for (src, token), q in self.tokens.items() if src == source}
107	
108	    def derivations_for(self, source: str) -> dict[str, str]:
109	        return {code: q for (src, code), q in self.derivations.items() if src == source}

111	
112	def _read(directory: Path, name: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
113	    with open(directory / name, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
114	        return list(csv.DictReader(f))
115	
116	
117	def _flag(text: str, where: str, problems: list[str]) -> bool:
118	    if text not in ("true", "false"):
119	        problems.append(f"{where}: expected true or false, got {text!r}")
120	    return text == "true"
121	
122	
123	def _digest(directory: Path) -> str:
124	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
125	    for name in FILES:
126	        digest.update(name.encode() + b"\0" + (directory / name).read_bytes() + b"\0")
127	    return digest.hexdigest()
128	
129	
130	def load(directory: Path | str = DICTIONARY_DIR) -> Dictionary:
131	    directory = Path(directory)
132	    problems: list[str] = []
133	
134	    nutrients: dict[str, Nutrient] = {}
135	    for r in _read(directory, "nutrients.csv"):
136	        if r["nutrient_id"] in nutrients:
137	            problems.append(f"nutrients.csv: duplicate nutrient_id {r['nutrient_id']}")
138	        if not r["unit"]:
139	            problems.append(f"nutrients.csv[{r['nutrient_id']}]: unit is empty")
140	        nutrients[r["nutrient_id"]] = Nutrient(r["nutrient_id"], r["infoods_tag"], r["name"],
141	                                               r["unit"], r["description"])
142	
143	    qualifiers: dict[str, Qualifier] = {}
144	    for r in _read(directory, "qualifiers.csv"):
145	        where = f"qualifiers.csv[{r['qualifier']}]"
146	        if r["qualifier"] in qualifiers:
147	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate")
148	        if r["amount_rule"] not in ("null", "required"):
149	            problems.append(f"{where}: amount_rule must be null or required")
150	        qualifiers[r["qualifier"]] = Qualifier(
151	            r["qualifier"], _flag(r["has_quantity"], where, problems),
152	            _flag(r["directly_observed"], where, problems), r["amount_rule"], r["description"])
153	
154	    groups: dict[str, LicenceGroup] = {}
155	    for r in _read(directory, "licence_groups.csv"):
156	        where = f"licence_groups.csv[{r['licence_group']}]"
157	        if r["licence_group"] in groups:
158	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate")
159	        groups[r["licence_group"]] = LicenceGroup(r["licence_group"], r["name"],
160	                                                  _flag(r["shippable"], where, problems),
161	                                                  r["description"])
162	
163	    sources: dict[str, Source] = {}
164	    for r in _read(directory, "sources.csv"):
165	        where = f"sources.csv[{r['namespace']}]"
166	        if r["namespace"] in sources:
167	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate")
168	        if r["licence_group"] not in groups:
169	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown licence group {r['licence_group']!r}")
170	        sources[r["namespace"]] = Source(r["namespace"], r["dataset_id"], r["name"], r["release"],
171	                                         r["licence"], r["licence_group"], r["attribution"], r["url"])
172	
173	    mappings: list[Mapping] = []
174	    seen_ids: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
175	    seen_priorities: set[tuple[str, str, int]] = set()
176	    for r in _read(directory, "nutrient_map.csv"):
177	        where = f"nutrient_map.csv[{r['source']} {r['source_nutrient_id']}]"
178	        try:
179	            priority = int(r["priority"])
180	        except ValueError:
181	            problems.append(f"{where}: priority {r['priority']!r} is not an integer")
182	            continue
183	        m = Mapping(r["source"], r["source_nutrient_id"], r["source_nutrient_name"], r["source_unit"],
184	                    r["nutrient_id"], priority, r["unit_conversion"],
185	                    r["numeric_qualifier_override"], r["notes"])
186	        if m.source not in sources:
187	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown source")
188	        nutrient = nutrients.get(m.nutrient_id)
189	        if nutrient is None:
190	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown nutrient {m.nutrient_id!r}")
191	        if (m.source, m.source_nutrient_id) in seen_ids:
192	            problems.append(f"{where}: mapped twice")
193	        seen_ids.add((m.source, m.source_nutrient_id))
194	        if (m.source, m.nutrient_id, m.priority) in seen_priorities:
195	            problems.append(f"{where}: priority {priority} repeated for {m.nutrient_id}")
196	        seen_priorities.add((m.source, m.nutrient_id, m.priority))
197	        if priority < 1:
198	            problems.append(f"{where}: priority must be 1 or more")
199	        if m.numeric_qualifier_override and m.numeric_qualifier_override not in qualifiers:
200	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown override qualifier {m.numeric_qualifier_override!r}")
201	        if m.unit_conversion not in UNIT_CONVERSIONS:
202	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown unit_conversion {m.unit_conversion!r}")
203	        elif nutrient is not None:
204	            conversion = UNIT_CONVERSIONS[m.unit_conversion]
205	            source_unit, canonical_unit = m.source_unit.lower(), nutrient.unit.lower()
206	            if conversion is None and source_unit != canonical_unit:
207	                problems.append(f"{where}: source unit {m.source_unit!r} is not {nutrient.unit!r} "
208	                                "and no unit_conversion is given")
209	            if conversion is not None and conversion != (source_unit, canonical_unit):
210	                problems.append(f"{where}: {m.unit_conversion} converts {conversion[0]} to "
211	                                f"{conversion[1]}, not {source_unit} to {canonical_unit}")
212	        mappings.append(m)
213	
214	    derivations: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
215	    for r in _read(directory, "derivation_qualifiers.csv"):
216	        where = f"derivation_qualifiers.csv[{r['source']} {r['code']!r}]"
217	        if r["source"] not in sources:
218	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown source")
219	        if r["qualifier"] not in qualifiers:
220	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown qualifier {r['qualifier']!r}")
221	        if (r["source"], r["code"]) in derivations:
222	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate")
223	        derivations[(r["source"], r["code"])] = r["qualifier"]
224	
225	    tokens: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
226	    for r in _read(directory, "value_tokens.csv"):
227	        where = f"value_tokens.csv[{r['source']} {r['token']!r}]"
228	        if r["source"] not in sources:
229	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown source")
230	        qualifier = qualifiers.get(r["qualifier"])
231	        if qualifier is None:
232	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown qualifier {r['qualifier']!r}")
233	        elif qualifier.amount_rule != "null":
234	            # A token carries no number. Mapping one to a qualifier that needs an
235	            # amount would force the pipeline to invent one — which is the bug.
236	            problems.append(f"{where}: a token may only map to a qualifier with no amount, "
237	                            f"not {r['qualifier']!r}")
238	        if r["token"] != r["token"].strip() or not r["token"]:
239	            problems.append(f"{where}: token must be non-empty and trimmed")
240	        if (r["source"], r["token"]) in tokens:
241	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate")
242	        tokens[(r["source"], r["token"])] = r["qualifier"]
243	
244	    if problems:
245	        raise DictionaryError(f"{len(problems)} problem(s) in {directory}:\n  " + "\n  ".join(problems))
246	    return Dictionary(nutrients, qualifiers, groups, sources, tuple(mappings), derivations, tokens,
247	                      _digest(directory))

1	"""Turning one source cell into (amount, qualifier) — Processing Design v0.1 §2.
2	
3	The most consequential bug available in this project is a one-line type
4	coercion that turns CoFID's `Tr` or `N` into 0. Every source goes through
5	`qualify`, which has no path from a non-numeric cell to a number other than
6	an explicit, bounded `< x`.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import math
11	import re
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	from typing import Any, Sequence
14	
15	KJ_PER_KCAL = 4.184  # thermochemical calorie
16	_DECIMAL = re.compile(r"[+-]?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?")
17	
18	
19	class UnrecognisedValue(ValueError):
20	    """A cell no rule covers. The stage fails rather than guess."""
21	
22	
23	class NegativeAmount(UnrecognisedValue):
24	    """A published number below zero — not a quantity. Never stored, never clamped to 0.
25	
26	    Source modules may catch this one case, emit no row, and record the cell in
27	    their manifest's notes.rejected_values (README "Qualifying a value").
28	    """
29	
30	
31	@dataclass(frozen=True)
32	class Qualified:
33	    amount: float | None
34	    qualifier: str
35	
36	
37	def parse_decimal(text: str, *, decimal_comma: bool = False) -> float | None:
38	    """A plain finite decimal, or None. Never NaN, never infinity, never a token."""
39	    s = text.strip()
40	    if decimal_comma and s.count(",") == 1 and "." not in s:
41	        s = s.replace(",", ".")
42	    if not _DECIMAL.fullmatch(s):
43	        return None
44	    number = float(s)
45	    return number if math.isfinite(number) else None
46	
47	
48	def qualify(cell: str, *, tokens: dict[str, str], numeric_override: str = "",
49	            derivation_qualifier: str = "", decimal_comma: bool = False,
50	            bound_prefix: str = "") -> Qualified:
51	    """The README's seven-step rule, in order. Blank cells never get here."""
52	    text = cell.strip()
53	    if not text:
54	        raise UnrecognisedValue("blank cell reached qualify(); a blank cell produces no row")
55	    if text in tokens:
56	        return Qualified(None, tokens[text])
57	    if bound_prefix and text.startswith(bound_prefix):
58	        bound = parse_decimal(text[len(bound_prefix):], decimal_comma=decimal_comma)
59	        if bound is None or bound <= 0:
60	            raise UnrecognisedValue(f"{cell!r}: a bound must be a positive number")
61	        return Qualified(bound, "below_loq")
62	    number = parse_decimal(text, decimal_comma=decimal_comma)
63	    if number is None:
64	        raise UnrecognisedValue(f"{cell!r} is neither a number nor a known token")
65	    if number < 0:
66	        raise NegativeAmount(f"{cell!r}: a nutrient amount cannot be negative")
67	    if number == 0:
68	        return Qualified(0.0, "zero_reported")
69	    if numeric_override:
70	        return Qualified(number, numeric_override)
71	    if derivation_qualifier:
72	        return Qualified(number, derivation_qualifier)
73	    return Qualified(number, "measured")
74	
75	
76	def convert(amount: float | None, conversion: str) -> float | None:
77	    if amount is None or not conversion:
78	        return amount
79	    if conversion == "kj_to_kcal":
80	        return amount / KJ_PER_KCAL
81	    raise ValueError(f"unknown unit conversion {conversion!r}")
82	
83	
84	def select(candidates: Sequence[tuple[int, Qualified, Any]]) -> tuple[int, Qualified, Any] | None:
85	    """One value where several source columns feed one canonical nutrient.
86	
87	    `candidates` are (priority, Qualified, payload). The lowest priority that
88	    carries a quantity wins; if none does, the lowest priority's marker is
89	    kept rather than dropped.
90	    """
91	    ordered = sorted(candidates, key=lambda c: c[0])
92	    for candidate in ordered:
93	        if candidate[1].qualifier != "not_analysed":
94	            return candidate
95	    return ordered[0] if ordered else None
96

1	"""Canonical rows (Processing Design v0.1 §2–§4) and the checks every stage runs on them."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import math
5	import re
6	from collections import Counter
7	from dataclasses import dataclass
8	from typing import Sequence
9	
10	from .dictionary import Dictionary
11	from .values import parse_decimal
12	
13	BASES = ("per_100g", "per_100ml")
14	_LANGUAGE = re.compile(r"[a-z]{2,3}")
15	
16	
17	@dataclass(frozen=True)
18	class Food:
19	    namespace: str
20	    local_id: str
21	    licence_group: str
22	    food_group_code: str
23	    food_group_name: str
24	    source_record: str
25	
26	    @property
27	    def food_ref(self) -> str:
28	        return f"{self.namespace}:{self.local_id}"
29	
30	
31	@dataclass(frozen=True)
32	class FoodName:
33	    food_ref: str
34	    language: str
35	    name: str
36	    is_primary: bool
37	
38	
39	@dataclass(frozen=True)
40	class Value:
41	    food_ref: str
42	    nutrient_id: str
43	    basis: str
44	    amount: float | None
45	    qualifier: str
46	    confidence: str
47	    source_value: str
48	    source_nutrient_id: str
49	    source_unit: str
50	    licence_group: str
51	
52	
53	def validate(foods: Sequence[Food], names: Sequence[FoodName], values: Sequence[Value],
54	             dictionary: Dictionary, *, namespace: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
55	    """Every rule a canonical row set must satisfy. An empty list means valid.
56	
57	    `namespace` confines the set to one source (the canonical stage); the
58	    union stage passes None and every row is checked against its own source.
59	    """
60	    problems: list[str] = []
61	
62	    foods_by_ref: dict[str, Food] = {}
63	    for f in foods:
64	        where = f"food {f.food_ref}"
65	        if namespace is not None and f.namespace != namespace:
66	            problems.append(f"{where}: namespace {f.namespace!r} in canonical/{namespace}")
67	        if f.namespace not in dictionary.sources:
68	            problems.append(f"{where}: namespace {f.namespace!r} is not in sources.csv")
69	            continue
70	        if not f.local_id or f.local_id != f.local_id.strip():
71	            problems.append(f"{where}: local_id must be non-empty and trimmed")
72	        if f.licence_group != dictionary.group_of(f.namespace):
73	            problems.append(f"{where}: licence group {f.licence_group!r}, but sources.csv says "
74	                            f"{dictionary.group_of(f.namespace)!r}")
75	        if f.food_ref in foods_by_ref:
76	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate food_ref")
77	        foods_by_ref[f.food_ref] = f
78	
79	    primaries: Counter[str] = Counter()
80	    seen_names: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
81	    for n in names:
82	        where = f"name {n.food_ref}/{n.language}"
83	        if n.food_ref not in foods_by_ref:
84	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown food")
85	        if not _LANGUAGE.fullmatch(n.language):
86	            problems.append(f"{where}: language must be a lower-case ISO 639 code")
87	        if not n.name.strip():
88	            problems.append(f"{where}: empty name")
89	        if (n.food_ref, n.language) in seen_names:
90	            problems.append(f"{where}: two names in one language")
91	        seen_names.add((n.food_ref, n.language))
92	        primaries[n.food_ref] += n.is_primary
93	    for ref in foods_by_ref:
94	        if primaries[ref] != 1:
95	            problems.append(f"food {ref}: {primaries[ref]} primary names, needs exactly 1")
96	
97	    seen_values: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
98	    for v in values:
99	        where = f"value {v.food_ref}/{v.nutrient_id}/{v.basis}"
100	        food = foods_by_ref.get(v.food_ref)
101	        if food is None:
102	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown food")
103	            continue
104	        if v.nutrient_id not in dictionary.nutrients:
105	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown nutrient")
106	        if v.basis not in BASES:
107	            problems.append(f"{where}: basis must be one of {BASES}")
108	        qualifier = dictionary.qualifiers.get(v.qualifier)
109	        if qualifier is None:
110	            problems.append(f"{where}: unknown qualifier {v.qualifier!r}")
111	        elif qualifier.amount_rule == "null" and v.amount is not None:
112	            problems.append(f"{where}: {v.qualifier} must have no amount, got {v.amount!r} "
113	                            "— a token is never coerced to a number")
114	        elif qualifier.amount_rule == "required" and v.amount is None:
115	            problems.append(f"{where}: {v.qualifier} requires an amount")
116	        if v.amount is not None and (not math.isfinite(v.amount) or v.amount < 0):
117	            problems.append(f"{where}: amount {v.amount!r} is not a finite non-negative number")
118	        if v.qualifier == "zero_reported" and v.amount != 0:
119	            problems.append(f"{where}: zero_reported with amount {v.amount!r}")
120	        # Independent of the qualifier logic: only a cell that says zero may become 0.
121	        if v.amount == 0 and parse_decimal(v.source_value, decimal_comma=True) != 0:
122	            problems.append(f"{where}: amount 0 from source cell {v.source_value!r} "
123	                            "— only an explicit zero may become 0")
124	        if not v.source_value.strip():
125	            problems.append(f"{where}: source_value is empty")
126	        if not v.source_nutrient_id or not v.source_unit:
127	            problems.append(f"{where}: source_nutrient_id and source_unit are required")
128	        if v.licence_group != food.licence_group:
129	            problems.append(f"{where}: licence group {v.licence_group!r} differs from its food's "
130	                            f"{food.licence_group!r}")
131	        key = (v.food_ref, v.nutrient_id, v.basis)
132	        if key in seen_values:
133	            problems.append(f"{where}: duplicate value")
134	        seen_values.add(key)
135	
136	    return problems
137

1	"""Reading and writing canonical row sets (README "Canonical format").
2	
3	The same three files describe processed/canonical/{namespace}/ and
4	processed/union/; only the manifest differs.
5	"""
6	from __future__ import annotations
7	
8	from collections import Counter
9	from pathlib import Path
10	from typing import Iterable, Sequence
11	
12	from .dictionary import Dictionary
13	from .lake import (read_csv, read_json, sha256_file, staged_directory, tool_revision, utc_now,
14	                   write_csv, write_json)
15	from .model import Food, FoodName, Value, validate
16	
17	ROW_FILES = ("foods.csv", "food_names.csv", "values.csv")
18	FOOD_COLUMNS = ["food_ref", "namespace", "local_id", "licence_group", "food_group_code",
19	                "food_group_name", "source_record"]
20	NAME_COLUMNS = ["food_ref", "language", "name", "is_primary"]
21	VALUE_COLUMNS = ["food_ref", "nutrient_id", "basis", "amount", "qualifier", "confidence",
22	                 "source_value", "source_nutrient_id", "source_unit", "licence_group"]
23	
24	
25	class CanonicalError(ValueError):
26	    """A row set breaks the contract. Nothing is written."""
27	
28	
29	def format_amount(amount: float | None) -> str:
30	    return "" if amount is None else repr(float(amount))
31	
32	
33	def parse_amount(text: str) -> float | None:
34	    return None if text == "" else float(text)
35	
36	
37	def raise_if_invalid(problems: Sequence[str], what: str) -> None:
38	    if problems:
39	        shown = "\n  ".join(problems[:30])
40	        more = f"\n  … and {len(problems) - 30} more" if len(problems) > 30 else ""
41	        raise CanonicalError(f"{what}: {len(problems)} problem(s)\n  {shown}{more}")
42	
43	
44	def counts(foods: Sequence[Food], names: Sequence[FoodName], values: Sequence[Value]) -> dict:
45	    return {
46	        "foods": len(foods),
47	        "names": len(names),
48	        "values": len(values),
49	        "values_by_nutrient": dict(sorted(Counter(v.nutrient_id for v in values).items())),
50	        "values_by_qualifier": dict(sorted(Counter(v.qualifier for v in values).items())),
51	        "values_by_basis": dict(sorted(Counter(v.basis for v in values).items())),
52	        "foods_without_values": len({f.food_ref for f in foods} - {v.food_ref for v in values}),
53	    }
54	
55	
56	def write_rows(directory: Path, foods: Iterable[Food], names: Iterable[FoodName],
57	               values: Iterable[Value]) -> dict[str, str]:
58	    """Writes the three row files in key order; returns their SHA-256s."""
59	    write_csv(directory / "foods.csv", FOOD_COLUMNS, (
60	        [f.food_ref, f.namespace, f.local_id, f.licence_group, f.food_group_code,
61	         f.food_group_name, f.source_record]
62	        for f in sorted(foods, key=lambda f: f.food_ref)))
63	    write_csv(directory / "food_names.csv", NAME_COLUMNS, (
64	        [n.food_ref, n.language, n.name, "1" if n.is_primary else "0"]
65	        for n in sorted(names, key=lambda n: (n.food_ref, n.language))))
66	    write_csv(directory / "values.csv", VALUE_COLUMNS, (
67	        [v.food_ref, v.nutrient_id, v.basis, format_amount(v.amount), v.qualifier, v.confidence,
68	         v.source_value, v.source_nutrient_id, v.source_unit, v.licence_group]
69	        for v in sorted(values, key=lambda v: (v.food_ref, v.nutrient_id, v.basis))))
70	    return {name: sha256_file(directory / name) for name in ROW_FILES}
71	
72	
73	def write_canonical(out_dir: Path, *, namespace: str, foods: Iterable[Food],
74	                    names: Iterable[FoodName], values: Iterable[Value], dictionary: Dictionary,
75	                    inputs: list[dict], notes: dict | None = None) -> dict:
76	    """Validates, then replaces `out_dir`. An invalid set leaves the old output untouched."""
77	    foods, names, values = list(foods), list(names), list(values)
78	    raise_if_invalid(validate(foods, names, values, dictionary, namespace=namespace),
79	                     f"canonical/{namespace}")
80	    source = dictionary.sources[namespace]
81	    with staged_directory(out_dir) as scratch:
82	        manifest = {
83	            "stage": "canonical",
84	            "namespace": namespace,
85	            "dataset_id": source.dataset_id,
86	            "release": source.release,
87	            "licence_group": source.licence_group,
88	            "dictionary_sha256": dictionary.sha256,
89	            "generated_at": utc_now(),
90	            "tool_revision": tool_revision(),
91	            "inputs": inputs,
92	            "outputs": write_rows(scratch, foods, names, values),
93	            "counts": counts(foods, names, values),
94	            "notes": notes or {},
95	        }
96	        write_json(scratch / "manifest.json", manifest)
97	    return manifest
98	
99	
100	def read_rows(directory: Path) -> tuple[list[Food], list[FoodName], list[Value]]:
101	    foods = []
102	    for r in read_csv(directory / "foods.csv"):
103	        food = Food(r["namespace"], r["local_id"], r["licence_group"], r["food_group_code"],
104	                    r["food_group_name"], r["source_record"])
105	        if r["food_ref"] != food.food_ref:
106	            raise CanonicalError(f"{directory}/foods.csv: food_ref {r['food_ref']!r} is not "
107	                                 f"namespace:local_id ({food.food_ref!r})")
108	        foods.append(food)
109	    names = [FoodName(r["food_ref"], r["language"], r["name"], r["is_primary"] == "1")
110	             for r in read_csv(directory / "food_names.csv")]
111	    values = [Value(r["food_ref"], r["nutrient_id"], r["basis"], parse_amount(r["amount"]),
112	                    r["qualifier"], r["confidence"], r["source_value"], r["source_nutrient_id"],
113	                    r["source_unit"], r["licence_group"])
114	              for r in read_csv(directory / "values.csv")]
115	    return foods, names, values
116	
117	
118	def read_canonical(directory: Path) -> tuple[list[Food], list[FoodName], list[Value], dict]:
119	    """Reads a row set and refuses it if any file changed after its manifest was written."""
120	    directory = Path(directory)
121	    manifest = read_json(directory / "manifest.json")
122	    for name in ROW_FILES:
123	        actual = sha256_file(directory / name)
124	        if manifest.get("outputs", {}).get(name) != actual:
125	            raise CanonicalError(f"{directory}/{name} does not match its manifest "
126	                                 "(edited after it was written?) — regenerate it")
127	    return (*read_rows(directory), manifest)

1	"""USDA FoodData Central, Foundation Foods — licence group A (CC0 1.0).
2	
3	The reference source module (README "Source rules"): `extract` copies the
4	in-scope rows in USDA's own shape; `canonicalise` applies dictionary/ and
5	nothing else.
6	"""
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import csv
10	import shutil
11	from collections import defaultdict
12	from pathlib import Path
13	
14	from ..canonical_io import CanonicalError, write_canonical
15	from ..dictionary import Dictionary
16	from ..lake import (Lake, read_csv, read_json, sha256_file, staged_directory, tool_revision,
17	                    utc_now, write_json)
18	from ..model import Food, FoodName, Value
19	from ..values import NegativeAmount, UnrecognisedValue, convert, qualify, select
20	
21	NAMESPACE = "usda"
22	MANIFEST = "usda"
23	RELEASE_FOLDER = "FoodData_Central_csv_2026-04-30"
24	DATA_TYPES = ("foundation_food",)
25	BASIS = "per_100g"  # FDC reports every nutrient amount per 100 g of food
26	SCOPED_TABLES = ("food.csv", "food_nutrient.csv", "food_portion.csv")
27	WHOLE_TABLES = ("foundation_food.csv", "nutrient.csv", "food_nutrient_derivation.csv",
28	                "food_category.csv", "measure_unit.csv")
29	CANONICAL_INPUTS = ("food.csv", "foundation_food.csv", "food_nutrient.csv", "nutrient.csv",
30	                    "food_nutrient_derivation.csv", "food_category.csv")
31	
32	
33	def _filter_rows(src: Path, dst: Path, keep) -> int:
34	    """Copies the header and every row `keep(row, column_index)` accepts. Cells untouched."""
35	    kept = 0
36	    with open(src, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fin, \
37	            open(dst, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fout:
38	        reader = csv.reader(fin)
39	        writer = csv.writer(fout, lineterminator="\n", quoting=csv.QUOTE_ALL)
40	        header = next(reader)
41	        writer.writerow(header)
42	        column = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(header)}
43	        for row in reader:
44	            if keep(row, column):
45	                writer.writerow(row)
46	                kept += 1
47	    return kept
48	
49	
50	def extract(lake: Lake) -> Path:
51	    inputs = lake.verify_inputs(MANIFEST, [f"{RELEASE_FOLDER}/{t}" for t in SCOPED_TABLES + WHOLE_TABLES])
52	    source = lake.source_dir(MANIFEST) / RELEASE_FOLDER
53	    out = lake.extracted(NAMESPACE)
54	    with staged_directory(out) as scratch:
55	        in_scope: set[str] = set()
56	
57	        def foundation(row, column):
58	            if row[column["data_type"]] in DATA_TYPES:
59	                in_scope.add(row[column["fdc_id"]])
60	                return True
61	            return False
62	
63	        rows = {"food.csv": _filter_rows(source / "food.csv", scratch / "food.csv", foundation)}
64	        for table in SCOPED_TABLES[1:]:
65	            rows[table] = _filter_rows(source / table, scratch / table,
66	                                       lambda row, column: row[column["fdc_id"]] in in_scope)
67	        for table in WHOLE_TABLES:
68	            shutil.copyfile(source / table, scratch / table)
69	        write_json(scratch / "manifest.json", {
70	            "stage": "extract",
71	            "namespace": NAMESPACE,
72	            "release": lake.manifest(MANIFEST)["release"],
73	            "data_types": list(DATA_TYPES),
74	            "generated_at": utc_now(),
75	            "tool_revision": tool_revision(),
76	            "inputs": inputs,
77	            "rows_kept": rows,
78	            "outputs": {p.name: sha256_file(p) for p in sorted(scratch.iterdir())},
79	        })
80	    return out
81	
82	
83	def canonicalise(lake: Lake, dictionary: Dictionary) -> dict:
84	    ext = lake.extracted(NAMESPACE)
85	    extracted = read_json(ext / "manifest.json")
86	    for name in CANONICAL_INPUTS:
87	        if extracted["outputs"].get(name) != sha256_file(ext / name):
88	            raise CanonicalError(f"{ext / name} changed after extraction; re-run `extract usda`")
89	    inputs = [{"file": f"processed/extracted/{NAMESPACE}/{name}", "sha256": extracted["outputs"][name]}
90	              for name in CANONICAL_INPUTS]
91	
92	    group = dictionary.group_of(NAMESPACE)
93	    listed = {r["fdc_id"] for r in read_csv(ext / "foundation_food.csv")}
94	    categories = {r["id"]: r for r in read_csv(ext / "food_category.csv")}
95	    derivation_codes = {r["id"]: r["code"] for r in read_csv(ext / "food_nutrient_derivation.csv")}
96	    units = {r["id"]: r["unit_name"] for r in read_csv(ext / "nutrient.csv")}
97	    mappings = dictionary.mappings_for(NAMESPACE)
98	    for maps in mappings.values():
99	        for m in maps:
100	            if units.get(m.source_nutrient_id) != m.source_unit:
101	                raise CanonicalError(f"nutrient_map.csv gives usda {m.source_nutrient_id} unit "
102	                                     f"{m.source_unit!r}; nutrient.csv says "
103	                                     f"{units.get(m.source_nutrient_id)!r}")
104	    tokens = dictionary.tokens_for(NAMESPACE)
105	    derivations = dictionary.derivations_for(NAMESPACE)
106	
107	    foods: list[Food] = []
108	    names: list[FoodName] = []
109	    excluded: list[dict] = []
110	    for row in read_csv(ext / "food.csv"):
111	        fdc_id = row["fdc_id"]
112	        if fdc_id not in listed:
113	            excluded.append({"fdc_id": fdc_id, "description": row["description"],
114	                             "publication_date": row["publication_date"],
115	                             "reason": "data_type foundation_food but not listed in "
116	                                       "foundation_food.csv (superseded or withdrawn record)"})
117	            continue
118	        category = categories.get(row["food_category_id"], {})
119	        food = Food(NAMESPACE, fdc_id, group, category.get("code", ""),
120	                    category.get("description", ""), f"food.csv fdc_id={fdc_id}")
121	        foods.append(food)
122	        names.append(FoodName(food.food_ref, "en", row["description"].strip(), True))
123	
124	    kept = {f.local_id for f in foods}
125	    mapped = {m.source_nutrient_id for maps in mappings.values() for m in maps}
126	    by_food: dict[str, dict[str, dict]] = defaultdict(dict)
127	    unmapped_duplicates: list[dict] = []
128	    for row in read_csv(ext / "food_nutrient.csv"):
129	        if row["fdc_id"] not in kept:
130	            continue
131	        if row["nutrient_id"] in by_food[row["fdc_id"]]:
132	            if row["nutrient_id"] in mapped:
133	                raise CanonicalError(f"usda:{row['fdc_id']} has two food_nutrient rows for nutrient "
134	                                     f"{row['nutrient_id']}; refusing to pick one")
135	            # Not canonicalised in this phase, so nothing is picked — but a reviewer should know.
136	            unmapped_duplicates.append({"fdc_id": row["fdc_id"], "nutrient_id": row["nutrient_id"],
137	                                        "food_nutrient_ids": [by_food[row["fdc_id"]][row["nutrient_id"]]["id"],
138	                                                              row["id"]]})
139	            continue
140	        by_food[row["fdc_id"]][row["nutrient_id"]] = row
141	
142	    values: list[Value] = []
143	    rejected: list[dict] = []
144	    for food in foods:
145	        published = by_food.get(food.local_id, {})
146	        for nutrient_id, maps in mappings.items():
147	            candidates = []
148	            for m in maps:
149	                row = published.get(m.source_nutrient_id)
150	                if row is None or not row["amount"].strip():
151	                    continue
152	                code = derivation_codes.get(row["derivation_id"]) if row["derivation_id"] else ""
153	                if code is None:
154	                    raise CanonicalError(f"{food.food_ref}: derivation_id {row['derivation_id']!r} "
155	                                         "is not in food_nutrient_derivation.csv")
156	                if code not in derivations:
157	                    raise CanonicalError(f"USDA derivation code {code!r} has no row in "
158	                                         "dictionary/derivation_qualifiers.csv")
159	                try:
160	                    qualified = qualify(row["amount"], tokens=tokens,
161	                                        numeric_override=m.numeric_qualifier_override,
162	                                        derivation_qualifier=derivations[code])
163	                except NegativeAmount:
164	                    # USDA publishes a negative "carbohydrate, by difference" where the other
165	                    # proximates sum past 100 g. Not a quantity: no row, and it is recorded.
166	                    rejected.append({"food_ref": food.food_ref, "source_nutrient_id": m.source_nutrient_id,
167	                                     "source_value": row["amount"], "reason": "negative amount"})
168	                    continue
169	                except UnrecognisedValue as error:
170	                    raise CanonicalError(f"{food.food_ref} nutrient {m.source_nutrient_id}: {error}") from error
171	                candidates.append((m.priority, qualified, (m, row, code)))
172	            chosen = select(candidates)
173	            if chosen is None:
174	                continue
175	            _, qualified, (m, row, code) = chosen
176	            values.append(Value(food.food_ref, nutrient_id, BASIS,
177	                                convert(qualified.amount, m.unit_conversion), qualified.qualifier,
178	                                code, row["amount"].strip(), m.source_nutrient_id,
179	                                units[m.source_nutrient_id], group))
180	
181	    return write_canonical(lake.canonical(NAMESPACE), namespace=NAMESPACE, foods=foods, names=names,
182	                           values=values, dictionary=dictionary, inputs=inputs,
183	                           notes={"data_types": list(DATA_TYPES), "excluded": excluded,
184	                                  "rejected_values": rejected,
185	                                  "unmapped_duplicates": unmapped_duplicates})
186

1	"""Source modules. Each defines NAMESPACE, extract(lake) and canonicalise(lake, dictionary).
2	
3	Discovered by name so that adding a source never edits a shared file.
4	"""
5	from __future__ import annotations
6	
7	import importlib
8	import pkgutil
9	from types import ModuleType

12	def load_sources() -> dict[str, ModuleType]:
13	    found: dict[str, ModuleType] = {}
14	    for info in pkgutil.iter_modules(__path__):
15	        if info.name.startswith("_"):
16	            continue
17	        module = importlib.import_module(f"{__name__}.{info.name}")
18	        found[module.NAMESPACE] = module
19	    return dict(sorted(found.items()))

18	def _summary(manifest: dict) -> str:
19	    c = manifest["counts"]
20	    return (f"{c['foods']} foods, {c['names']} names, {c['values']} values; "
21	            f"qualifiers {json.dumps(c['values_by_qualifier'])}")
22	
23	
24	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
25	    sources = load_sources()
26	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="almanac_nutrition", description=__doc__)
27	    parser.add_argument("--lake", help="food-data lake root "
28	                                       "(default: $ALMANAC_FOOD_DATA or ~/ALManac-food-data)")
29	    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
30	    for name in ("extract", "canonicalise"):
31	        commands.add_parser(name).add_argument("source", choices=sorted(sources))
32	    commands.add_parser("union")
33	    commands.add_parser("bundle")
34	    commands.add_parser("all", help="extract and canonicalise every source, then union and bundle")
35	    commands.add_parser("fixture", help="regenerate fixtures/bundle_v1.sql for AlmanacCore's tests")
36	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
37	
38	    lake = Lake(args.lake)
39	    try:
40	        dictionary = load()
41	        if args.command == "extract":
42	            print(f"extracted {args.source} -> {sources[args.source].extract(lake)}")
43	        elif args.command == "canonicalise":
44	            print(f"canonical {args.source}: {_summary(sources[args.source].canonicalise(lake, dictionary))}")
45	        elif args.command == "union":
46	            print(f"union: {_summary(bundle.union(lake, dictionary))}")
47	        elif args.command == "fixture":
48	            print(f"fixture -> {fixture.write(dictionary)}")
49	        elif args.command == "bundle":
50	            report = bundle.build(lake, dictionary)
51	            print(f"bundle {report['path']} ({', '.join(report['namespaces'])}): "
52	                  f"{report['rows_checked']} rows passed the licence assertion; sha256 {report['sha256']}")
53	        else:
54	            for namespace, module in sources.items():
55	                module.extract(lake)
56	                print(f"canonical {namespace}: {_summary(module.canonicalise(lake, dictionary))}")
57	            print(f"union: {_summary(bundle.union(lake, dictionary))}")
58	            report = bundle.build(lake, dictionary)
59	            print(f"bundle {report['path']}: {report['rows_checked']} rows passed the licence "
60	                  f"assertion; sha256 {report['sha256']}")
61	    except FAILURES as error:
62	        print(f"FAILED: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
63	        return 1
64	    return 0

# Almanac — Processing Design v0.1

**Status:** design only. `processed/` is empty and stays empty until a stage
below is deliberately executed.
**Date:** 2026-09-01 · Phase 16 lifted the same day.
**Inputs:** `DATASETS.csv`, `LICENSES.md`, and Technical Specification v1.0
(48-table iOS/SQLite schema, HealthKit sync, provenance enums in Slice 1).

---

## 1. The constraint that drives everything else

Almanac ships as an iOS app with an on-device SQLite database. That single fact
converts the licensing analysis from paperwork into architecture:

> **Putting a food row in the app bundle is redistributing it to every user who
> installs the app.**

Not "using" it. Not "referencing" it. Redistributing — to an unbounded audience,
commercially, in a form they keep on their device. This is the strictest
possible reading of every licence in `LICENSES.md`, and it is the correct one.

Three consequences fall straight out:

| | Rule |
|---|---|
| **Group A + B** | May ship inside the app bundle. Attribution obligations travel with them. |
| **Group C** (ODbL) | Must **never** enter the bundle. Share-alike would attach to the shipped database itself. |
| **Group D** | Must **never** enter the bundle. Includes all five FAO datasets, SFDA, Bahrain ×2, INNTA, IFCT, NEVO, TBCA. |

**What actually ships in v1** is therefore already decided, and it is not small:

| Dataset | Licence | Foods |
|---|---|---:|
| USDA FoodData Central | CC0 1.0 | 2,101,280 |
| ANSES-CIQUAL 2025 | CC BY 4.0 + Etalab 2.0 | 3,484 |
| CoFID 2021 | OGL v3.0 | 2,887 |
| AFCD Release 3 | CC BY 4.0 | 1,588 |
| **Total** | | **~2.11 M** |

Frida (CC BY 4.0) joins this tier the moment it is downloaded. Nothing here
waits on a single reply to a single email.

### The trap to design against
The failure mode is not "we ship ODbL data by accident on day one." It is:
someone adds SFDA dishes to make Saudi search work, six months of user data
accumulates against those food IDs, and then the rights answer comes back "no".
At that point the data cannot be removed by deleting rows — user log entries
point at it, and the export the user downloads contains it.

**So the boundary is enforced structurally, not by discipline.** A licence group
is a column on every food row and a filter on the bundle build, and the build
fails loudly rather than shipping a mixed database.

---

## 2. Per-value provenance, because all four sources already have it

This is the discovery from surveying the files, and it changes the schema.

Every one of the four clean sources ships quality metadata **per nutrient
value** — in four incompatible vocabularies:

| Source | What it carries per value |
|---|---|
| **USDA** | `derivation_id`, `data_points`, `min`/`max`/`median`, `loq`, `min_year_acquired` |
| **CIQUAL** | `code_confiance` (A–D confidence), `source_code`, optional `min`/`max` |
| **CoFID** | `Tr` (trace), `N` (not analysed) tokens **in the value cell itself** |
| **AFCD** | `Derivation` column: `Borrowed`, `Recipe`, analysed |

Concretely, the proximates sheet of CoFID alone carries **4,101 `Tr` and 2,874
`N`** values. The naive pipeline casts those to float, gets `NaN`, and writes
`0` or `NULL`.

Both are wrong, and wrong in a way that matters to a body-monitor product:

- `Tr` means *present in trace amounts* — not zero.
- `N` means *nobody measured it* — not zero, and not "absent".

Rendering "not analysed" as **0 mg of iron** tells a user their intake is zero
when the truth is unknown. That is the single most consequential bug available
in this entire project, and it is introduced by a one-line type coercion.

### The value model
A nutrient value is therefore never a bare number:

```
nutrient_value(
  food_ref,            -- namespaced, see §3
  nutrient_id,         -- canonical
  amount              REAL     NULL,   -- NULL only when genuinely unmeasured
  qualifier           TEXT     NOT NULL,
  confidence          TEXT     NULL,   -- source's own grade, verbatim
  source_value        TEXT     NOT NULL,-- the original cell, unparsed
  source_nutrient_id  TEXT     NOT NULL,
  source_unit         TEXT     NOT NULL,
  licence_group       CHAR(1)  NOT NULL
)
```

`qualifier` is a closed enum — the spec's Slice 1 already calls for provenance
enums, so this lands in existing plans:

`measured` · `trace` · `not_analysed` · `below_loq` · `borrowed` ·
`calculated_recipe` · `calculated_factor` · `zero_reported`

Note `zero_reported` is distinct from `trace` and from `not_analysed`. Three
different facts that a float column collapses into one.

`source_value` is the reversibility guarantee: whatever the parser gets wrong,
the original cell is still there to re-derive from without returning to `raw/`.

---

## 3. Identifiers — namespace, never renumber

```
usda:1105904      ciqual:1000      cofid:13-145      afcd:F002258
```

Source identifiers are stable, published, and cited in the literature. An
Almanac-internal integer key is a private detail that must never replace them.
Namespacing costs a few bytes and buys three things: a food is always traceable
to its publisher, two sources can be held side by side without collision, and
**removing a whole source stays a one-line delete** — which is exactly what a
"no" from a rights holder will require.

Almanac-native records get their own namespace, `almanac:`, and are the only
rows Almanac owns outright (per `LICENSES.md`, "What Almanac may license
independently").

---

## 4. Units — two traps

**Trap 1: per 100 g vs per 100 mL.** AFCD ships these as *separate sheets*
(`All solids & liquids per 100 g`, `Liquids only per 100 mL`) because they are
not interchangeable. Merging them into one `per_100` column silently corrupts
every liquid. The basis is a column, not an assumption.

**Trap 2: the density database is Group D.** Converting household measures
("1 cup") to mass is core to the product, and the obvious tool — the FAO/INFOODS
Density Database, 6,565 records — carries *"all rights reserved"* with no
standing grant. It cannot ship.

The workable substitute is already in hand and is CC0: USDA's `food_portion`
table maps `fdc_id` + `measure_unit` → `gram_weight` directly, with 47,446 rows,

import re
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Iterator

from lxml import etree

from ..dictionary import Dictionary

    "alim_grp_2025_11_03.xml": "ALIM_GRP",
    "compo_2025_11_03.xml": "COMPO",
    "const_2025_11_03.xml": "CONST",
    "sources_2025_11_03.xml": "SOURCES",
}

                ("alim_ssgrp_code", "alim_ssgrp_nom_eng"),
                ("alim_grp_code", "alim_grp_nom_eng"))

ALIM_GRP_COLUMNS = tuple(column for level in GROUP_LEVELS for column in level)

COMPO_COLUMNS = ("alim_code", "const_code", "teneur", "code_confiance")

def csv_name(xml_name: str) -> str:

def _records(path: Path, record_element: str) -> Iterator[tuple[list[str], list[str], list[tuple[str, str]]]]:

    Streams with iterparse and frees each record once read. Anything the CSV
    could not represent — another element, nesting, text outside a cell, an
    attribute other than `missing`, a missing cell that has text — fails the
    stage rather than being dropped.
    """
    depth = 0
    number = 0
    for event, element in etree.iterparse(str(path), events=("start", "end"), resolve_entities=False,
                                          no_network=True, load_dtd=False):

                                     f"expected <{ROOT_ELEMENT}><{record_element}><cell/>…")
            continue

        if depth != 1:  # cells are read from their record; the root needs nothing
            continue
        number += 1
        where = f"{path.name}: <{record_element}> #{number}"
        if element.attrib or (element.text or "").strip():
            raise CanonicalError(f"{where} has attributes or text of its own")

        cells: list[str] = []
        absent: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        for cell in element:
            if not isinstance(cell.tag, str) or len(cell) or (cell.tail or "").strip():
                raise CanonicalError(f"{where} holds something other than flat cells")
            text = (cell.text or "").strip()
            unexpected = sorted(set(cell.attrib) - {"missing"})
            if unexpected:
                raise CanonicalError(f"{where} <{cell.tag}> has attribute(s) {unexpected}")
            if "missing" in cell.attrib:
                if text:
                    raise CanonicalError(f"{where} <{cell.tag}> is marked missing but says {text!r}")

            names.append(cell.tag)
            cells.append(text)
        yield names, cells, absent

        while element.getprevious() is not None:
            del element.getparent()[0]

    """Writes one CSV column per cell element, in the source's order. Returns what it saw."""
    columns: list[str] | None = None
    rows = 0
    markers: dict[str, Counter[str]] = defaultdict(Counter)
    with open(dst, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f, lineterminator="\n", quoting=csv.QUOTE_ALL)
        for names, cells, absent in _records(src, record_element):
            if columns is None:
                if len(set(names)) != len(names):
                    raise CanonicalError(f"{src.name}: a <{record_element}> repeats an element: {names}")
                columns = names
                writer.writerow(columns)
            elif names != columns:
                raise CanonicalError(f"{src.name}: <{record_element}> #{rows + 1} has elements {names}; "
                                     f"the first record has {columns}")
            writer.writerow(cells)
            for name, marker in absent:
                markers[name][marker] += 1
            rows += 1
    if columns is None:
        raise CanonicalError(f"{src.name} holds no <{record_element}> records")
    return {"record_element": record_element, "rows": rows, "columns": columns,
            "missing_markers": {name: dict(sorted(m.items())) for name, m in sorted(markers.items())}}


def extract(lake: Lake) -> Path:

    source = lake.source_dir(MANIFEST)
    out = lake.extracted(NAMESPACE)

        tables = {csv_name(xml): {"source": xml, **_extract_table(source / xml, element, scratch / csv_name(xml))}
                  for xml, element in TABLES.items()}
        write_json(scratch / "manifest.json", {
            "stage": "extract",
            "namespace": NAMESPACE,
            "release": lake.manifest(MANIFEST)["release"],
            "generated_at": utc_now(),
            "tool_revision": tool_revision(),
            "inputs": inputs,
            "tables": tables,
            "outputs": {p.name: sha256_file(p) for p in sorted(scratch.iterdir())},

    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        lacking = [c for c in required if c not in (reader.fieldnames or [])]
        if lacking:
            raise CanonicalError(f"{path.name} has no column(s) {lacking}; re-run `extract {NAMESPACE}`")
        yield from reader


def _is_placeholder(code: str) -> bool:
    return set(code) <= {"0"}  # "", "00", "0000", "000000"


def _group_names(rows: Iterable[dict[str, str]]) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    """alim code column -> {code: English name}, one name per code, placeholders named '-'."""
    names: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {code_column: {} for code_column, _ in GROUP_LEVELS}
    for row in rows:
        for code_column, name_column in GROUP_LEVELS:
            code, name = row[code_column], row[name_column]
            known = names[code_column].setdefault(code, name)
            if known != name:
                raise CanonicalError(f"{ALIM_GRP}: {code_column} {code} is named both {known!r} and {name!r}")
    for code_column, by_code in names.items():
        for code, name in by_code.items():
            if _is_placeholder(code) != (name == PLACEHOLDER_GROUP_NAME) or not name:
                raise CanonicalError(f"{ALIM_GRP}: {code_column} {code!r} is named {name!r}; expected codes "
                                     f"of zeros, and only those, to be named {PLACEHOLDER_GROUP_NAME!r}")
    return names


def _food_group(row: dict[str, str], groups: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """The most specific group level that is not a placeholder, with its English name."""
    for code_column, _ in GROUP_LEVELS:
        code = row[code_column]
        if _is_placeholder(code):
            continue
        name = groups[code_column].get(code)
        if name is None:
            raise CanonicalError(f"alim_code {row['alim_code']}: {code_column} {code!r} is not in {ALIM_GRP}")
        return code, name
    return "", ""


def _check_units(mappings: dict, constituents: dict[str, dict[str, str]]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Each mapped const_code exists, states the dictionary's unit, and is per 100 g."""
    checked = {}
    for maps in mappings.values():
        for m in maps:
            const = constituents.get(m.source_nutrient_id)
            if const is None:
                raise CanonicalError(f"nutrient_map.csv maps ciqual {m.source_nutrient_id}, which is not in {CONST}")
            stated = _UNIT.search(const["const_nom_eng"])
            if stated is None:
                raise CanonicalError(f"{CONST}: const_code {m.source_nutrient_id} ({const['const_nom_eng']!r}) "
                                     "states no unit")
            unit, per = stated.group(1).strip(), re.sub(r"\s+", "", stated.group(2))
            if unit != m.source_unit:
                raise CanonicalError(f"nutrient_map.csv gives ciqual {m.source_nutrient_id} unit {m.source_unit!r}; "
                                     f"{CONST} says {const['const_nom_eng']!r}")
            if per != BASIS_DENOMINATOR:
                raise CanonicalError(f"{CONST}: const_code {m.source_nutrient_id} ({const['const_nom_eng']!r}) is "
                                     f"per {per!r}, not per {BASIS_DENOMINATOR}; values would not be {BASIS}")
            checked[m.source_nutrient_id] = const["const_nom_eng"]
    return dict(sorted(checked.items()))


def canonicalise(lake: Lake, dictionary: Dictionary) -> dict:
    ext = lake.extracted(NAMESPACE)
    if not (ext / "manifest.json").is_file():
        raise CanonicalError(f"{ext} has no manifest.json; run `extract {NAMESPACE}` first")
    extracted = read_json(ext / "manifest.json")
    for name in CANONICAL_INPUTS:
        recorded = extracted.get("outputs", {}).get(name)
        if recorded is None or not (ext / name).is_file() or recorded != sha256_file(ext / name):
            raise CanonicalError(f"{ext / name} is missing or changed after extraction; "
                                 f"re-run `extract {NAMESPACE}`")
    inputs = [{"file": f"processed/extracted/{NAMESPACE}/{name}", "sha256": extracted["outputs"][name]}
              for name in CANONICAL_INPUTS]

    group = dictionary.group_of(NAMESPACE)
    mappings = dictionary.mappings_for(NAMESPACE)
    mapped = {m.source_nutrient_id for maps in mappings.values() for m in maps}
    constituents = {r["const_code"]: r for r in _read(ext / CONST, CONST_COLUMNS)}
    checked_units = _check_units(mappings, constituents)
    groups = _group_names(_read(ext / ALIM_GRP, ALIM_GRP_COLUMNS))
    tokens = dictionary.tokens_for(NAMESPACE)

    foods: list[Food] = []
    names: list[FoodName] = []
    without_group: list[str] = []
    line_breaks: list[dict] = []
    for row in _read(ext / ALIM, ALIM_COLUMNS):
        code = row["alim_code"]
        if not code:
            raise CanonicalError(f"{ALIM}: a food has no alim_code")
        if any(f.local_id == code for f in foods[-1:]) or code in {f.local_id for f in foods}:
            # compo refers to foods by alim_code alone, so a repeated code leaves its values unattributable.
            raise CanonicalError(f"{ALIM}: alim_code {code} appears twice; compo values could not be attributed")
        group_code, group_name = _food_group(row, groups)
        food = Food(NAMESPACE, code, group, group_code, group_name, f"{ALIM_XML} alim_code={code}")
        foods.append(food)
        if not group_code:
            without_group.append(food.food_ref)
        if not row["alim_nom_eng"]:
            raise CanonicalError(f"{food.food_ref} has no alim_nom_eng for its primary name")
        for language, column, primary in (("en", "alim_nom_eng", True), ("fr", "alim_nom_fr", False)):
            if row[column]:
                names.append(FoodName(food.food_ref, language, row[column], primary))
                if "\n" in row[column] or "\r" in row[column]:
                    line_breaks.append({"food_ref": food.food_ref, "language": language, "name": row[column]})

    kept = {f.local_id for f in foods}
    published: dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, str]]] = defaultdict(dict)
    pairs: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    for row in _read(ext / COMPO, COMPO_COLUMNS):
        pair = (row["alim_code"], row["const_code"])
        if pair in pairs:
            raise CanonicalError(f"{COMPO} has two rows for alim_code {pair[0]} const_code {pair[1]}; "
                                 "refusing to pick one")
        pairs.add(pair)
        if row["const_code"] not in mapped:
            continue
        if row["alim_code"] not in kept:
            raise CanonicalError(f"{COMPO}: alim_code {row['alim_code']} is not in {ALIM}")
        published[row["alim_code"]][row["const_code"]] = row

    values: list[Value] = []
    rejected: list[dict] = []
    blank = 0
    for food in foods:
        cells = published.get(food.local_id, {})
        for nutrient_id, maps in mappings.items():
            candidates = []
            for m in maps:
                row = cells.get(m.source_nutrient_id)
                if row is None:
                    continue
                if not row["teneur"].strip():
                    blank += 1  # the source says nothing: no row
                    continue
                try:
                    qualified = qualify(row["teneur"], tokens=tokens, decimal_comma=True, bound_prefix="<",
                                        numeric_override=m.numeric_qualifier_override)
                except NegativeAmount:
                    rejected.append({"food_ref": food.food_ref, "source_nutrient_id": m.source_nutrient_id,
                                     "source_value": row["teneur"].strip(), "reason": "negative amount"})
                    continue
                except UnrecognisedValue as error:
                    raise CanonicalError(f"{food.food_ref} const_code {m.source_nutrient_id}: {error}") from error
                candidates.append((m.priority, qualified, (m, row)))
            chosen = select(candidates)
            if chosen is None:
                continue
            _, qualified, (m, row) = chosen
            values.append(Value(food.food_ref, nutrient_id, BASIS,
                                convert(qualified.amount, m.unit_conversion), qualified.qualifier,
                                row["code_confiance"], row["teneur"].strip(), m.source_nutrient_id,
                                m.source_unit, group))

    return write_canonical(lake.canonical(NAMESPACE), namespace=NAMESPACE, foods=foods, names=names,
                           values=values, dictionary=dictionary, inputs=inputs,
                           notes={"basis": f"{BASIS}, as every mapped const_nom_eng states",
                                  "mapped_constituents": checked_units,
                                  "blank_cells": blank,
                                  "rejected_values": rejected,
                                  "foods_without_food_group": without_group,
                                  "names_with_line_breaks": line_breaks})
